assertion_results.text: Epics are generated between Feature and Tasks — at least 2 Epics are created (one per repository) when by-repository grouping is used
assertion_results.evidence: The impact-map.md documents 'Grouping strategy: by-repository' and creates two Epics: 'Epic: TC-9006: trustify-backend' (Tasks 1-2) and 'Epic: TC-9006: trustify-ui' (Tasks 3-6). The summary-comment.md confirms 'Total: 2 Epics, 6 Tasks'.

assertion_results.text: Each Epic summary follows the format '<feature-key>: <repository-name>' (e.g., 'TC-9006: trustify-backend', 'TC-9006: trustify-ui')
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md line 43: 'Epic: TC-9006: trustify-backend' and line 52: 'Epic: TC-9006: trustify-ui'. Both follow the '<feature-key>: <repository-name>' format exactly.

assertion_results.text: Each task specifies its parent Epic key in the output — tasks targeting trustify-backend are assigned to the backend Epic, tasks targeting trustify-ui are assigned to the frontend Epic
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md lists Tasks 1-2 under 'Epic: TC-9006: trustify-backend' (lines 49-50) and Tasks 3-6 under 'Epic: TC-9006: trustify-ui' (lines 53-56). summary-comment.md explicitly maps each task to its parent Epic in the tables: Tasks 1-2 have 'Parent Epic: TC-9006: trustify-backend' and Tasks 3-6 have 'Parent Epic: TC-9006: trustify-ui'.

assertion_results.text: The plan documents Incorporates links from the Feature to each Epic (not from Feature to individual Tasks) — evidenced by link decisions in the impact map or task output files
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md lines 65-68: 'Incorporates (Feature to Epics)' section states 'TC-9006 incorporates Epic "TC-9006: trustify-backend"' and 'TC-9006 incorporates Epic "TC-9006: trustify-ui"'. Line 69 explicitly notes: 'Incorporates links go from Feature to Epics only, not from Feature to individual Tasks.'

assertion_results.text: Task dependency ordering is preserved within and across Epics — backend tasks have lower task numbers than dependent frontend tasks
assertion_results.evidence: Backend tasks are Task 1 and Task 2. Frontend tasks are Tasks 3-6. impact-map.md lines 72-76 show dependency chain: Task 2 depends on Task 1, Task 3 depends on Tasks 1 and 2, Task 4 depends on Task 3, Task 5 depends on Task 4, Task 6 depends on Tasks 1-5. Backend tasks (1,2) have lower numbers than all frontend tasks (3-6), and frontend tasks depend on backend tasks being complete.

assertion_results.evidence: Non-doc tasks 1-5 all contain: Repository, Target Branch, Description, Files to Modify and/or Files to Create, Implementation Notes, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. Task 1: Repository (trustify-backend), Target Branch (main), Description, Files to Modify (2 files), Files to Create (8 files), Implementation Notes, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. Task 2: all sections present. Task 3: all sections present. Task 4: all sections present. Task 5: all sections present. Task 6 (documentation task, filename 'task-6-remediation-documentation.md'): contains Repository (trustify-ui), Target Branch (main), Description, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements — exempt from Files to Modify/Create and Implementation Notes as a documentation task.

assertion_results.text: Convention-aware enrichment validates file-type applicability per shared/convention-applicability-rules.md before including a convention — inapplicable conventions are excluded entirely (not listed with 'Not applicable' annotations), and applicable ones include a rationale in the prescribed format ('Applies: task modifies <file> matching the convention's <scope>'), not free-form prose
assertion_results.evidence: All Implementation Notes sections in tasks 1-5 include conventions with the prescribed rationale format. Examples: Task 1: 'Applies: task creates `modules/remediation/src/model/summary.rs` matching the convention's Rust module file scope.' Task 2: 'Applies: task creates `modules/remediation/src/endpoints/by_product.rs` matching the convention's .rs endpoint file scope.' Task 3: 'Applies: task modifies `src/api/rest.ts` matching the convention's .ts API file scope.' Task 4: 'Applies: task creates `src/pages/RemediationDashboardPage/RemediationDashboardPage.tsx` matching the convention's .tsx page component scope.' Task 5: 'Applies: task creates `src/pages/RemediationDashboardPage/components/VulnerabilityTable.tsx` matching the convention's .tsx component scope.' No 'Not applicable' annotations found in any task file. All rationales follow the prescribed format naming specific files and scopes. Task 6 (documentation) has no Implementation Notes section and thus no convention annotations, which is appropriate for its exemption.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a priority set (not 'Undefined'), the plan documents that the Feature's priority is inherited by created tasks — evidenced by priority field values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When the Feature's priority is 'Undefined', the plan documents that priority inheritance is skipped (not propagated as null or 'Undefined')
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md line 80: 'Priority: "High" — inherited from Feature TC-9006 and propagated to all Epics and Tasks via additional_fields.priority.' Lines 86-93 show Task Creation Log with additional_fields including '"priority": {"name": "High"}' for all tasks and Epics. summary-comment.md line 42: 'Priority: "High" — propagated from Feature TC-9006 to all Epics and Tasks. The Feature's priority is set (not "Undefined"), so it is included in additional_fields.priority on every created issue.'

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a non-empty fixVersions array and the fixVersion scope config (from ### Jira Field Defaults in CLAUDE.md) is 'task' or 'both' (or absent, defaulting to 'both'), the plan documents that fixVersions are inherited by created tasks — evidenced by fixVersion values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When fixVersion scope is 'feature' or the Feature has no fixVersions, the plan documents that fixVersion inheritance is skipped
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md line 81: 'fixVersions: ["RHTPA 1.5.0"] — inherited from Feature TC-9006 and propagated to all Epics and Tasks via additional_fields.fixVersions. The fixVersion scope setting is not present in CLAUDE.md Jira Field Defaults, defaulting to "both" (propagate to tasks).' Lines 86-93 show Task Creation Log with additional_fields including '"fixVersions": [{"name": "RHTPA 1.5.0"}]'. summary-comment.md line 43 confirms the same with explicit reasoning about the default scope.

assertion_results.text: A summary of inherited field propagation is produced — evidenced by a summary-comment.md file in the outputs directory, or a summary section in the impact map that includes the inherited priority and fixVersion values propagated to tasks, or states they were omitted and why
assertion_results.evidence: summary-comment.md exists in the outputs directory and contains an 'Inherited Field Values' section (lines 40-44) documenting: 'Priority: "High" — propagated from Feature TC-9006 to all Epics and Tasks' and 'fixVersions: ["RHTPA 1.5.0"] — propagated from Feature TC-9006 to all Epics and Tasks' with explanations of why each was propagated. The impact-map.md also has a 'Field Inheritance' section (lines 79-82) and a 'Task Creation Log — additional_fields' section (lines 84-93) documenting the same.
